notes.title: Dev Diary #6: Missions in Last Train Home
notes.notes:
Welcome to our sixth [b]Dev Diary[/b]! Join us for an exclusive behind-the-scenes look into the development of [b]Last Train Home[/b], a survival strategy game centered on the Czechoslovak Legionaries and their challenging odyssey following the Great War. In this edition, we shine a spotlight on in-game [b]Missions[/b].  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237776/fc80105f98ce7eff8aa89429d51210bf7c8800d5.jpg[/img]

[h3]Dozens of handcrafted missions [/h3]

Last Train Home uniquely combines[b] real-time missions[/b] with a [b]tactical pause feature[/b] and [b]train management[/b]. It includes nearly 40 missions, and the game spans 40+ hours on average. All of the mission maps are meticulously [b]handcrafted [/b]and, therefore, [b]unique[/b].  

In the main game, you assume command of [b]small squads of soldiers[/b], ranging from a minimum of three to a maximum of ten members. We intended to emphasize the individuality of each soldier, reflected not only in combat but also in train management.   

Your soldiers are equipped with [b]Combat Roles[/b], such as Machine Gunners, Medics, Riflemen, Grenadiers, and Scouts. Each profession possesses a unique skill set. That means you must carefully consider each member's abilities when composing the squad and navigating the challenges ahead.  

Additionally, our recently launched DLC, [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2617710/Last_Train_Home__Legion_Tales/]Legion Tales[/url], introduces an extra ten missions, further expanding the game's depth and [b]replayability[/b]. In the DLC, you embark on missions with pre-set narrative squads and gradually unlock new selectable challenges for them to conquer.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237776/1f186a61df609ee624c4ac3d6d28ba0267af8374.jpg[/img]

[h3]Types of missions & quests [/h3] 

Last Train Home features [b]various mission types[/b] to keep you engaged and challenged. Some missions revolve around defending or capturing specific objects, while others focus on sabotage, aiding civilians, or carrying out assassinations. Additionally, a few missions are centered on stealth gameplay, requiring players to utilize mechanics such as [b]Silent Mode[/b] and [b]Concealment [/b]to navigate and succeed.   

However, most missions in Last Train Home are [b]multifaceted[/b], blending various types of main and side objectives to offer a rich and dynamic gameplay experience. For instance, you may start by aiding villagers in repairing fences and carrying heavy boxes, only to later receive a main quest to eliminate enemy soldiers. Optional objectives allow you to make progress in the main quests easier or earn valuable resources as rewards. 

Additionally, we intend to inspire you to [b]explore the maps [/b]further by concealing numerous loot opportunities. Certain loot caches are strategically placed behind locked gates, enticing you to engage in thorough exploration and complete quests to unlock them. This approach provides tangible rewards for players who invest time and effort into thoroughly exploring the game world.  

An intriguing aspect of the development process is that each [b]Level Designer[/b] takes ownership of their missions, resulting in a [b]distinct signature style[/b] infused into the game. Some focus on realistic military scenarios, while others highlight civilian suffering. Despite these differences, a clear standard ensures players can navigate all missions easily. 

[h3]First designs [/h3]

The Level Designers dedicated extensive effort to crafting mission designs and refining various gameplay mechanics, collaborating closely with [b]Technical Designers[/b] and [b]Programmers [/b]to bring these visions to life.  

Coordination with the [b]Art Department [/b]was also crucial in the development process. Based on thorough research, the Level Design team created detailed [b]wishlists [/b]outlining the necessary models for each mission, such as diverse building types. In most cases, [b]placeholders [/b]were initially utilized, allowing for seamless integration until the Art department created the final models.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237776/ec4ba84f0eca3a986735f6fcf92962445663fefb.jpg[/img]

For example, one of the significant tasks in our model creation process was to develop a large set of objects designed to function as [b]cover elements[/b], as the core gameplay revolves around strategic positioning and movement between those points.  

Every object ranging in height from [b]30 centimeters to 1.5 meters[/b] was crafted to serve as a cover. We classify them into two main types: [b]soft [/b]and [b]hard[/b]. Soft covers include objects that are relatively easy to shoot through, such as thin wooden fences or boxes. Conversely, hard cover consists of things resistant to gunfire, such as boulders or sandbags. These distinctions are visually represented by their respective [b]icons[/b], providing clear indicators during gameplay.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237776/b5fbd7cd1349745effdd5500cc54f275261f4817.jpg[/img]

[h3]Evolution[/h3]  

Since the start of development, the missions underwent significant [b]transformations[/b]. Initially, the plan was to create an extensive collection of short missions with simple objectives, intending to reuse maps for multiple missions. However, as development progressed, we shifted towards crafting [b]unique and detailed maps for each mission[/b], aiming to make them more [b]immersive [/b]and [b]engaging[/b].  

Integrating new mechanics drove the evolution of missions and features into the game. As soldiers gained additional skills for battles, missions became more [b]complex[/b], requiring players to employ strategic thinking and utilize available features effectively.  

We experimented with different [b]sizes of maps[/b], too. Initially, missions were designed on larger maps to accommodate more units. However, as we adjusted their number to optimize gameplay, we correspondingly [b]scaled down [/b]the size of the maps. This adaptation ensured that missions remained enjoyable and engaging.  

A significant change to the mission gameplay was the introduction of the [b]Fog of War[/b], which was uniquely designed to introduce exploration mechanics. Thanks to this feature, you must [b]explore and reveal the maps piece by piece[/b]. It also enabled quests such as 'explore the designated part of the city' and similar objectives.  

Another important addition was the introduction of [b]Silent Mode[/b], which aimed to restrict enemy awareness and prevent them from being omniscient. This addition wasn't intended to force players into stealth gameplay throughout the mission but rather to provide them with strategic options and varied approaches to completing objectives. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237776/041c70209f76c3e86b96beafd58187b4c5961d36.jpg[/img]

[h3]Challenges of the environment [/h3] 

Transitioning from working on first-person shooters to a different genre posed [b]a notable challenge[/b] for most of our Level Designers. It required a shift in focus to accommodate the game's [b]isometric view[/b].  

Designers had to ensure that most elements were visible from the [b]default camera angle[/b], minimizing the need for camera rotation. This influenced various aspects of level design, such as [b]spacing between buildings[/b] and consideration of [b]verticality[/b]. For instance, the number of stories in buildings, height differences in terrain, and foliage density were adjusted to streamline gameplay and reduce complexity.  

As for the depiction of cities and villages in Last Train Home, it leans towards a romanticized aesthetic. As mentioned in the [url=https://steamcommunity.com/ogg/1469610/announcements/detail/3718340776827673776?snr=2___]Dev Diary dedicated to Worldbuilding[/url], adjusting the real environment for gameplay was necessary. For instance, abundant vegetation and fences were added to enrich the visual experience and provide strategic elements despite not being common during the era.  

Furthermore, the game offers diverse environments, ensuring you encounter varied landscapes as you progress. In addition to villages and cities, you can explore airports, factories, enemy camps, and fortifications.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237776/3fdeed7d8566a3d863556a240c09938a47677125.jpg[/img]

[h3]Three gameplay tips by the Level Designers [/h3]  

[olist]
[*] Players often resort to frequent [b]save loading,[/b] but it's not always necessary. For instance, reloading a save isn't the only solution when an alarm is triggered. Often, a simple change in approach, such as seeking cover, can resolve the situation.  

[*] It's not necessary to eliminate every enemy on the map. Sometimes, it's more advantageous to [b]evade [/b]them altogether.  

[*] [b]A thorough exploration[/b] of missions is encouraged, as alternative routes and strategies may offer better outcomes. The most direct or obvious path isn't always optimal, so experimentation and creativity are crucial to success. 
[/olist]

notes.title: Challenge yourself: A short guide to AI Mission Modifiers in Last Train Home
notes.notes:
[h3]Hello, Legionaries! [/h3]

We're excited to share a [b]practical guide[/b] detailing the [b]Mission Modifiers[/b] incorporated into Last Train Home. If you haven't noticed, you can now adjust [b]Information Sharing[/b],[b] Loud Noise[/b], and [b]Proximity Awareness [/b]distances and intensify enemy behavior this way. Tinkering with these settings will make the gameplay more challenging and force you to try different mission approaches.  

However, there are some [b]implications [/b]you need to consider. In this article, you will learn about the areas influenced by these modifiers and [b]a tip on configuring them effectively.[/b] 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237776/791d3c7423b5251cc02d74cf5de8b545d2a451b7.png[/img]
 
[h2]Loud noise  [/h2]

Loud noise is one of the primary methods of [b]enemy perception[/b]. It always comes from a specific source (e.g., in the case of a rifle, it is where the shot came from) and is heard by everyone within a particular range. While this range is set to [b]100 %[/b], it equals [b]36 meters[/b]. Setting it to [b]200 %[/b] means all units within [b]72 meters[/b] will hear the shot and run to investigate this place. A [b]question mark[/b] is displayed above their heads in this state. 

[h2]Information sharing  [/h2]

When enemies enter a combat state, indicated by an [b]exclamation mark[/b] above them (signifying their engagement with the player's forces), they signal nearby comrades within the information-sharing distance to join the fight. This range differs among units but averages around [b]25 meters[/b]. Doubling this value to [b]200 % [/b]means that when an enemy initiates combat, they rally their allies within a [b]50-meter radius[/b]. However, specific units, such as officers, can alert reinforcements as far as [b]70 meters[/b] away. 

[h2]Proximity awareness radius [/h2]

The proximity awareness radius is represented by a [b]small red circle[/b] that surrounds the enemy soldier when hovered over. Within this circle, enemies will immediately detect the player's units, even those in concealment. Typically, its width averages around [b]2 meters[/b]. Doubling it to [b]200 % [/b]generally expands it to [b]4 meters[/b]. Consequently, executing a stealth kill becomes unfeasible without additional abilities.  

[h2]Facts to consider [/h2]

[list]
[*] If set to extremes, loud noise, and information-sharing distance adjustments can have [b]unexpected consequences[/b]. They can cause various complications, such as being stuck in a mission, unable to complete a quest, or summoning enemies from previously inaccessible parts of the map into battle. 
[*] Proximity awareness is safe to play with but keep in mind that it makes completing the two stealth-kill-focused tutorial side quests at the beginning of the game nearly impossible. 
[/list]

[b] If you want to try amping up the combat difficulty with these modifiers, our Lead Level Designer recommends setting Loud noise to 120 %, Information Sharing to 120 %, and Proximity Awareness to 200 %[/b].

We hope you will find this short guide helpful. Give the new settings a try and let us know how it worked for you!

notes.title: Last Train Home - Update 3.0 - Patch notes
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237776/4157c994882f1e6281ef22d9db85cf087ebc8fe3.png[/img]

[h3]Greetings, Legionaries! [/h3]

We're excited to inform you about the third update for Last Train Home. This patch includes many bug fixes and balancing based on your valuable feedback. We sincerely appreciate your time and effort in reporting bugs and sharing your opinions about the game! Enjoy the update! 

[h2]Update 3.0 - Patch Notes[/h2] 

[h3]Major fixes [/h3]
- Problems happening after [b]save/load:[/b] 
[list]
[*] Empty vehicles are no longer suddenly becoming hostile. 
[*] Squad info refreshes correctly.  
[*] Coal for heating is consumed only when it should be. 
[*] The train can properly leave the station it has already visited. 
[/list]
- Text Event following the end of [b]Chany mission[/b] and [b]Drunk Driver[/b] Text Event do not block progress in the game.  
- Sudden [b]item duplication[/b] in train management is no longer happening.
- Machine gunners' [b]Suppressive Fire skill [/b]works properly. 
- Healing and the Stabilize skill used on a [b]downed soldier[/b] work properly.  
- It is better communicated that the [b]Stealth Kill[/b] can’t be used in close succession. 
- [b]Rifle Ammo Bag[/b] research now applies not only to Riflemen, but also to Scouts and Grenadiers. 
- [b]Tanks[/b] are able to hit even if the target is fairly close. 
- The [b]explosive barrels [/b]no longer explode after they have been already destroyed. 


[h3]Additions and improvements[/h3]
 - Improvements in the [b]Edit Squad Screen [/b]to achieve better communication of relevant Soldier Traits 
[list]
[*] Added: Beneficial Traits Filter that provides an idea of who you should select for the deployment.  
[*] Enabled: Point of Interest screen element is visible in Edit Squad Screen for better overview. 
[*] Added: Highlight of soldiers when hovering over Beneficial Traits. 
[/list]
- Added: [b]Attack Ground command[/b], thanks to which is now possible to target ground with artillery vehicles. 

[h3]Mission-related fixes[/h3]
[list]
[*] [b]Vladivostok[/b]: The issue of disappearing ammo for soldiers in trucks after loading the game is fixed. Soldiers can reload properly from the shared stash. 
[*] [b]Sukhinichi[/b]: Sudden mission failure following killing a civilian is no longer happening. 
[*] [b]Canyon[/b]: All the new soldiers get rescued correctly no matter which exit area is used. 
[*] [b]Barabinsk[/b]: Bridge explosions at the beginning moved and timed in a way that player- controlled units shouldn’t be harmed by them. 
[*] [b]Pisky[/b]: ‘Patchwork Makes Dream Work’ challenge now works properly. 
[/list]
[b][i]Note: While mission-specific issues were fixed, we recommend that you replay such missions from the beginning and do not load a previously created in-mission save where you experienced the problem.[/i][/b] 

[h3]Balancing changes[/h3]
[list]
[*] Balancing of the [b]frequency and timing of punishing events[/b] in train management. There should be fewer harsh events happening in a short period of time and in starting segments. 
[*] Balancing of [b]Traits impact[/b] (Herbalist, Hunter) on resource gathering in Points of Interest (lakes, forests, villages). 
[*] Balancing of [b]Operational Damage[/b] on train cars and respective [b]Endurance upgrades[/b] (Improved Leaf Springs, Metal Plating, Advanced Framing). Train cars now receive damage from a traveled distance, and it should feel more beneficial to make Endurance upgrades. 
[*] Balancing of [b]metal costs [/b]on car upgrades, fixing car statuses, research and crafting recipes. 
[*] Balancing done to make [b]ammo crafting[/b] less expensive. 
[/list]
[h3]DLC-specific fixes and improvements (spoilers included)[/h3]
- [b]Narrative squads[/b] balancing and tweaks: 
[list]
[*] All narrative squads now should have at least two soldiers with Stabilize or Heal skills and should feel stronger while playing the missions.  
[*] Profession levels were increased together with attributes to improve soldiers’ health, weapon handling, range of throwable skills (e. g. throwing a grenade). 
[/list]
- [b]Our Efforts/The Baikal Story:[/b]
[list]
[*] The ‘Massacre’ challenge can be finished as intended. 
[*] The armored car can no longer be entered to avoid unexpected explosions. 
[*] The playable area no longer locks back after getting to the pier. 
[*] Added: Covers in important locations.
[/list]  
[b]- Czech Revolutionary/The Incident Story:[/b]  
[list]
[*] The mission is finishable even without completing ‘Save the civilian’ challenge.  
[*] ‘Smooth and cool’ challenge now works properly. 
[/list] 
[b]- Our Company/The Blockade Story: [/b] 
[list]

[/list]

[list]
[*] Soldiers and tanks no longer disappear at the edge of the map; making it possible to leave the mission properly. 
[/list]
[b]- Barlie/The Cat Story: [/b]
[list]
[*] The falling rocks no longer block the way out.

[h3]Other fixes and polishes[/h3]

notes.title: Frostpunk meets Commandos in brutally realistic new strategy game
notes.notes:
Sometimes, a game comes along that feels like the combination of several of my personal all-time favorites. I'm a sucker for Command and Conquer, especially the original, Tiberian Dawn. Likewise, the cruel, punishing strategy of Frostpunk, and the small-scale, squad-driven RTS combat of XCOM and Commandos constitute some of my most-beloved gaming experiences ever. I like grounded strategy, hard-fought battles, and a pronounced sense of stakes and drama. I also prefer games with a sharper edge, that take on more somber and adult subject matter. Out now on Steam, Last Train Home is one of this year's most exciting new strategy games. Combining the best elements from Frostpunk, Command and Conquer, and the rest, it's available to try for free right now.

notes.title: Dev Diary #5: Combat in Last Train Home
notes.notes:
[h2]Dear Legionaries, [/h2]

Welcome to our fifth [b]Dev Diary[/b], offering a behind-the-scenes look into the development of [b]Last Train Home[/b], a survival strategy game that revolves around the Czechoslovak Legionaries and their arduous journey back home after the Great War. This edition will focus on [b]Combat[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237776/107618492013b69048896b0962810a5fdb978616.jpg[/img]

[h3]Embarking on the Journey [/h3]

Last Train Home presents a single-player, story-driven experience that spans approximately 40 to 50 hours. The game uniquely combines[b] train management [/b]and missions that contain [b]real-time combat[/b] with a [b]tactical view[/b] feature pausing the game.  

Within the world of Last Train Home, you take charge of [b]compact squads of soldiers[/b], ranging from a minimum of three to a maximum of ten members. Your soldiers are equipped with distinct [b]Combat Roles[/b], such as Machine Gunners, Medics, Riflemen, Grenadiers, and Scouts. Each profession possesses a unique skill set, which can be further honed and expanded according to your strategic choices.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237776/f59d78635e29a6aa3c85ef7fc2f5f4ce064bad09.jpg[/img]

[h3]Mastering Tactical Warfare [/h3]

These specialized skills are designed for specific situational challenges. Consequently, it's essential not to impulsively charge into battle but to thoughtfully assess both the [b]positioning [/b]of your soldiers and the [b]skillsets [/b]you can leverage to effectively address the current scenario. 

To achieve success, waiting for battles to self-resolve simply isn't an option; you must proactively engage in conflict resolution and maneuver the situation in your favor. Scouting, planning, and strategic positioning are vital to the [b]survival of your soldiers[/b]. 
 
Fortunately, you wield an arsenal of tools to influence battle outcomes, including the use of [b]Tactical View[/b]. During missions, you can pause the action by hitting the Space Bar, allowing you to issue move commands with ease or observe previously given orders. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237776/d494aba8f73bbaa6eb14a0ac205a98e0545173a6.jpg[/img]

[h3]Cover System [/h3]
Another vital mechanic is the cover system. Soldiers can take cover in positions that offer [b]partial protection [/b]while allowing them to shoot. Properly leveraging the terrain and various objects can shield your soldiers from incoming fire, although they remain vulnerable to flank attacks, rear assaults, and melee strikes. 

In-game covers are fully [b]procedurally generated[/b], with two types: soft cover and hard cover. [b]Soft cover[/b] offers limited protection, reducing the chance of being hit by 40%, while [b]hard cover [/b]provides substantial protection, reducing the chance of being hit by 80%. 

[h3]Silent Mode [/h3]
Last Train Home incorporates a Silent Mode, allowing your troops to move in a silent manner and even execute a stealth kill. However, [b]it's not intended as the primary solution[/b] for all situations. Some missions can be completed without firing a shot, but these are exceptions. In most cases, it's more effective to use Silent Mode for preparation or to set traps before switching to direct fire.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237776/c74aeef5a97f79d0c3b24cd69a714557af7f5402.jpg[/img]

[h3]Weapons and Equipment [/h3]
Your units can acquire three types of weapons, each with two possible ‘upgrades.’ You can purchase them from merchants or occasionally obtain them through the narrative. In addition to firearms, you can utilize landmines, grenades, and sleep flasks. However, all ammunition and equipment are limited, requiring [b]careful management [/b]for each mission. 
 
The game also features a powerful [b]artillery strike[/b] that can eliminate even well-fortified enemy positions. However, its use is restricted and subject to specific conditions. And be cautious, as enemies also have access to this potent weapon.

[h3]Health [/h3]

In pursuit of adding a sense of [b]persistence [/b]to the game, health doesn't regenerate automatically; you must heal your soldiers. Furthermore, healing during missions is temporary, and upon returning to the train, you must complete the healing process. Think of it as follows: a quick bandage won't fully heal a gunshot wound, and [b]recovery takes time[/b].

When a soldier's HP is depleted during a mission, they fall into a [b]downed state[/b], from which you can still save them. However, this safety net comes with consequences, as downed soldiers have a high chance of incurring permanent physical or mental damage, which cannot be reversed and accumulates over time, potentially making them a burden to the squad. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237776/2a7bfab69185895dfbd0b37a534012fbe9c836c8.jpg[/img] 

[h3]Beware of the Enemy [/h3] 
Enemies are categorized into [b]three types[/b], each with distinct statistics, skills, behavior, and attire. Additionally, they have access not only to regular weaponry but also to [b]armored vehicles[/b], posing a significant threat. 
 
In order to enhance the challenge and immersion of combat, we've developed an [b]AI system[/b] that empowers enemies to assess the battlefield dynamically, relying on probabilities to drive their actions. In contrast to many RTS titles, the AI system in Last Train Home is fairly advanced, with each unit making [b]independent decisions[/b]. This system strives to mimic the reactions of real-life soldiers, which, to be honest, presented a significant challenge for us. 
 
The enemies engage in calculated decisions, choosing the opportune moments to open fire, seek cover, switch positions, retreat, or attempt to outflank your troops. Their reactions are shaped by [b]visual [/b]and [b]auditory cues[/b], and they are guided by a sophisticated system encompassing numerous evaluative factors, aiding them in selecting their next target. To anticipate the adversaries' next moves, keen observation becomes indispensable. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237776/521ba4555bdaf6708c693fd05edf0ba166600977.jpg[/img]

[h3]Experience Points (XP) [/h3]
Your soldiers earn experience by completing objectives, but there are no rewards for killing enemies. XPs are used to [b]level up their roles[/b], enhancing specific attributes or unlocking new skills. Soldiers can even have multiple Combat Roles and combine their skills as long as the skill is not specific to a role or a weapon.  

[h3]Difficulty [/h3]

Regarding combat difficulty, the game offers a wide range of adjustments, allowing you to modify different statistics, such as damage inflicted on your troops and the enemies. However, the number of enemies and their behavior cannot be changed, as missions are pre-set and meticulously handcrafted. 

If our combat system has captured your interest, you can download the demo of Last Train Home on our[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1469610/Last_Train_Home/] Steam page [/url]now and try it for yourself. The full game is set for release on [b]November 28[/b]! 

Thank you for your attention, and stay tuned for more updates.

notes.title: Frequently Asked Questions about Last Train Home #2
notes.notes:
[h2]Hello, Legionaries! [/h2]

Thanks to all who submitted questions about [b]Last Train Home[/b] for last week's [b]Ask Me Anything (AMA) session[/b]. We've assembled the responses and invite you to delve into them. If you have any more questions, please don't hesitate to contact us through the comments section or on our [url=https://discord.gg/lasttrain]Discord server[/url].
 
[h2]History [/h2]

[h3]Why did the Czechoslovak Legionaries have to go East and not West? [/h3]

The situation was complex. When Russia entered World War I on the side of the Allies, the Czechoslovak Legionaries joined the Russian army and fought alongside the Russians against the Central Powers (including Austria-Hungary). This allowed them to actively contribute to the Allied war effort and promote their own cause for independence. 

Although the initial plan was for the Czechoslovak Legion to join the Western Front, logistical and political challenges, such as the blockade of the Western Front by the Central Powers, made it more feasible for them to fight on the Eastern Front.  
 
The Czechoslovak Legionaries' decision to go east was influenced, amongst other things, by the Brest-Litovsk Treaty, which was signed in March 1918. This treaty marked Russia's exit from World War I and resulted in the cession of vast territories, including Ukraine, Belarus, and the Baltics, to the Central Powers. As a consequence, the Legionaries found themselves in a precarious situation in the new territories controlled by the Central Powers. To escape captivity or persecution, they continued their eastward journey through Siberia, with the hope of eventually reaching the Western Front and fighting alongside the Allies to secure Czechoslovak independence. 

They had to travel a roughly 9000-kilometer-long expanse of the Trans-Siberian Railway. Following this demanding overland journey, they successfully secured passage on ships, enabling them to reach the United States, subsequently Europe, and, ultimately, their cherished homeland.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237776/4fde2f04c67186bdc58005f97d3dd15dfb863cfb.png[/img]

[h2]Historical accuracy, realism [/h2]

[h3]To what extent does the game stick with historical events? [/h3]
The game is inspired by historical events, it’s not their recreation. We have consulted the affairs with experts on the topic. Nevertheless, certain artistic liberties have been taken in various aspects of the game. 

For example, the events take roughly 6 months of in-game time, but in reality, it was 5 years. We concentrated the events in a smaller time frame, and thanks to that, the players can experience the critical points of that era. For more in-depth information, please refer to our Dev Diary available at this [url=https://thqn.net/3DRtTfl]link[/url]. 

[h3]When choosing weapons for the game, did you go by what felt interesting or historical sources?[/h3]
In this regard, the Association of Czechoslovak Legionaries provided valuable guidance as they conducted thorough research on the subject matter. Thanks to their efforts, we can affirm that the weaponry featured in the game was indeed accessible in Russia during that historical period. While certain arms may have been considered rare, they were nonetheless present. 

[h3]What level of realism are you targeting for combat? 
[/h3]
The level of combat realism is somewhat limited. Keep in mind that we are developing a game that needs to be accessible and enjoyable for the players. Furthermore, we want the players to be able to actively engage and freely maneuver, not just stick to one place and wait for the attrition to come.  To achieve this objective, we have made strategic adjustments to combat dynamics, including modifications to weapon ranges, ensuring a dynamic and engaging gaming experience. 

[h3]You mentioned how there were factories, schools, etc., set up along the line historically - will we be able to stop at these sites along the way and pick the Legionaries up? 
[/h3]
 
During your journey aboard the train, you will encounter various stops along the railway, providing opportunities to explore not only mission locations but also visit an array of Points of Interest, including villages, lakes, and forests. While building the world of Last Train Home, we were partially sticking to history. For a more in-depth understanding of our development process in this regard, we invite you to explore our [url=https://thqn.net/lth-dd04]fourth Dev Diary[/url], which delves into this topic further. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237776/5f0f15a5dc670ddd4835e5c25135d90414a7ff95.jpg[/img] 

[h2]Inspiration/ideas 
[/h2]

[h3]Which games was Last Train Home inspired by? 
[/h3]
Our creative process drew inspiration from a rich tapestry of sources. Notably, we looked at titles such as Frostpunk for insights into base management and the welfare of its inhabitants, Company of Heroes for real-time combat dynamics, and Starcraft 2 for user interface design. However, it's worth mentioning that some of the most significant sources of inspiration were the collective experiences of our team members, including their contributions to past projects like the UFO series developed by Altar Games. 

[h3]How did you come up with the idea to combine train management with RTS? 
[/h3]
We were drawn to the concept of extending player responsibilities beyond mission scenarios, involving the care of their squad and the management of their base, which is a similar concept to the UFO series. Furthermore, we aspired to introduce a strong element of persistence within the game, where the loss of soldiers becomes a permanent event, akin to the mechanics found in titles like Original War. Merging missions with the overarching management enables players to witness the lasting repercussions of their actions, thus emphasizing the pivotal role of persistence within the gameplay dynamics. 

[h2]Factions [/h2]

[h3]Will the White Army be included in the game? What about other factions? 
[/h3]
We made a deliberate choice to feature only the most formidable forces of this historical chapter, which include the Czechoslovak Legion, the Red Army, the White Army, and their respective sub-factions. 

[h3]Will there be Czech Legions from other countries than Russia (e.g., French and Italian) also be represented in any way? 
[/h3]
While it is true that the Czechoslovak Legionaries were dispersed across the globe, for us there was no way to connect those forces with the legionaries in Russian territory. Placing, for instance, Czechoslovak Legionaries stationed in Italy aboard a train in Russia would not align with historical context or coherence. 

[h2]Live action 
[/h2]

[h3]The live-action intermezzos are adapted from an actual movie, TV series, or was it filmed solely for the game? [/h3]
The live-action footage was exclusively filmed for our project. In the development of our trailers, we formed a partnership with Gnomon Production, a Czech film production company, and enlisted the expertise of Randis Albion, Senior Art Director at THQ Nordic, who assumed the role of Director of Photography. We anticipate the release of several additional feature trailers in the near future, and we encourage you to stay tuned for more exciting content. 

[h2]Replayability 
[/h2]

[h3]Will the storyline be linear, or do you plan with different storylines and different ends? 
[/h3]
The main narrative inherently adheres to a linear structure, given its fundamental objective of progressing from point A to point B along a railway with a couple of turnouts. However, there are several turnings that can change the gameplay – thanks to them, you can experience different missions, and face different threats and challenges. The final battle is also influenced greatly by the decisions you make during your journey. Furthermore, players will have the chance to immerse themselves in a range of smaller stories, designed to offer a comprehensive reflection of the wartime experience in its entirety. 

[h3]What (if any) degree of randomization will there be throughout the campaign? 
[/h3]
The core storyline remains consistent, as mentioned earlier. All of the missions are handcrafted and, therefore, unique. It's worth emphasizing that in Last Train Home, the quality and quantity go hand in hand, as the average journey onboard spans a gripping 40 hours.   

You have the option to replay the game, explore alternative routes, and experience missions you haven't encountered previously and also different text events. Even within the Points of Interest, a degree of randomization is applied. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237776/b4d47a978314f19a9e6914c9be65ef1c5bd3ac33.png[/img]

[h2]Features [/h2]

[h3]Are there game mechanics you were initially planning for the game but had to let go at some point? 
[/h3] 
Certainly, that is the pure nature of game development. In our initial concept, the game was intended to be roguelike, where players would strive to progress as far as possible and then restart. However, we came to the realization that this approach did not align with our overarching concept. Given that the game offers approximately 40 hours of gameplay, it would not be conducive to the player's experience to require a complete restart in a later segment due to prior mistakes. Consequently, our focus shifted toward emphasizing narrative elements and constructing distinct chapters that function as individual puzzles within the broader framework of the game. 

[h3]Will there be special "heroes” that you can deploy as squad leaders or something like that? Will you be able to make normal troops into heroes if they have lots of experience? 
[/h3]
With a limited number of soldiers on the train and the challenge of replacing them, every soldier onboard becomes a hero in their own right. As they gain experience, they acquire a variety of skills and the ability to take on multiple roles. For instance, a soldier can become both a medic and a machine gunner, harnessing the unique perks of each profession to their advantage. 

[h3]Will there be a way to remove negative traits as troops gain experience? 
[/h3]
For some of them, it’s possible. It also depends on what you see as negative or positive, as certain traits have their pros and cons.  

[h3]If your engine breaks down and can’t be fixed, can you seize or obtain another engine to pull your train? 
[/h3]
A malfunctioning locomotive represents one of the multiple pathways leading to a game-over scenario. 

[h2]Trains [/h2]

[h3]Is the train/locomotive seen in the game an actual train that existed, or is it inspired by one?  
[/h3]
In the game, you'll encounter three distinct locomotives, each drawing inspiration from real-world counterparts: the Grandpa, the Hound, and the Towing Bull. The same goes even for specific train cars.  

[h3]How many wagons can the Towing Bull pull at maximum upgrade? 
[/h3]
After the upgrade, it’s 9 wagons and the locomotive. 

[h3]Is there any chance of a whistle mechanic being woven into the game? 
[/h3]
Yes. And if you find out how to trigger it, you’ll even get an achievement.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237776/9ea3cd75b925861586b6bc9366739da44925cb4a.jpg[/img]

[h2]Demo [/h2]

[h3]Is it possible to import the progress from the demo to the full game? 
[/h3]
This is something we didn’t consider because the demo and the full game are, in fact, two different applications. However, for those curious to experiment, it's possible to attempt transferring saves since they are stored on your computer. We can't provide assurances that this method will function seamlessly, though. 

Furthermore, it's essential to keep in mind that we are continually fine-tuning the game. Consequently, the initial experience upon the game's release will differ and you will miss all the improvements we've integrated if you rely on an older save. 

[h3]What percentage of the full game does the demo represent? 
[/h3]
If you consider the length of the railway, the demo encompasses roughly 10 percent. To put it into perspective, the complete Trans-Siberian Railway spans 9,000 kilometers, with the playable segment in the demo extending to approximately 800 kilometers. In terms of missions, the demo provides a taste of 6 out of the total 40 missions available in the full game. 

[h3]For how long will the demo be available? 
[/h3]
The demo will stay available at least until the release of the full game. We’re planning to even update the demo with fixes based on the feedback we got during the Steam Next Fest.  

[h3]Who is Barbora Hlavatá or what role does she have? She's not in the encyclopedia. 
[/h3]
Barbora serves as an NPC within the game, assuming the role of one of the advisors available to you during the challenging voyage to Vladivostok – together with Major Gazdik, Captain Langer, and Jozef Levý. All of them advise you remotely rather than participating in the crew's active missions. Consequently, Barbora is not featured in the game's encyclopedia, which exclusively includes the profiles of controllable soldiers actively engaged in the missions. 

[h3]Will the crew be randomized? 
[/h3]
No, all of the soldiers are pre-set, and each of them is unique. They have their own bios, traits and abilities.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237776/4745cd1112c5154f607cea21976016ea969cb57f.jpg[/img]

[h2]Localization [/h2]

[h3]Are you planning to add new languages to the game? 
[/h3]
At the game's launch, players will have access to a comprehensive selection of 11 text languages. Additionally, the game offers full voice-overs in English, German, and French. For those seeking a deeper immersive experience, the ‘Immersion’ audio mode is available, featuring audio in Czech, Slovak, and Russian. As of now, there are no immediate plans to introduce additional languages. 

[h2]Stores, price 
[/h2]
[h3]How much will the game cost?  
[/h3]
39,99 EUR/USD 

[h3]Via which digital stores will the game sell? 
[/h3]
You’ll be able to buy the game on Steam and GOG, but also on others like: Amazon, Buka, CE Asia, Enaza, Focus Multimedia, Gamersgate, Games Republic, Gamestop, GreenMan Gaming, H2 Interactive, HeyBox Qing Feng, Humblebundle, Igratos Gamazavr, IndieGala, MacGame Store, Metaboli, Nexway, Nuuvem, Phoenix Fengxia, VoidU, Zetaprime, Ztorm.

[/h3]
Physical copies of the game will be made accessible through various retailers, please check this list for a couple of examples of retailers: Amazon Germany, Amazon UK, Amazon France, and other selected retailers in Austria (mediamarkt), Czech Republic (Alza, JRC, Xzone), France (FNAC, MircoMANIA), and Germany (GameStop, mediamarkt, Saturn). Not available in the US and Australia/New Zealand.

The physical edition will come bundled with additional materials, and we encourage you to stay tuned for forthcoming details and updates.

[h3]Will the game be available on Geforce Now? 
[/h3]
Yes.

[/h3]

notes.title: Addressing concerns related to optimization of Last Train Home
notes.notes:
[h2]Hi, Legionaries, [/h2]

We would like to formally address the [b] issues related to optimization [/b]that were reported to us via different channels during the [b]Steam Next Fest[/b].  

First and foremost, [b]thank you for playing the demo[/b] of Last Train Home and getting back to us with your feedback. It’s very valuable to us in enhancing the game's performance and user experience. 
 
The issues some of you faced include:

[list]
[*] [b]Crashes, freezes, severe FPS drops, and prolonged loading times when trying to start a new journey.[/b] - It seems these issues happen for specific architectures and combinations of graphic settings. We are thankful for every report via [url=https://redmine.thqnordic.com/news/26]Redmine [/url]as they help us track these issues and come up with solutions. But we'd also like to point out that during the Steam Next Fest, only [b]0.5 percent of the player base encountered crashes[/b].
[*] [b]FPS drops, freezes, and even crashes during gameplay [/b]– It seems this happens more often when using more monitors, especially when they have substantially different types of graphics cards and are handled by different built-in tools. Also, when putting the game in the background often and using certain combinations of graphics settings.
[*] [b]Memory leaks when playing for many hours with lots of save/load. [/b]
[/list]

[h3]What can you do? [/h3]

[list]
[*] Before downloading the demo, make sure to check the [b]minimal hardware requirements [/b]for playing the game on our [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1469610/Last_Train_Home/]Steam page[/url].  
[*] Make sure all your [b]drivers [/b]are up to date (AMD, Nvidia, Windows Updates...).  
[*] If you encounter any issues, bugs, or crashes, while playing the demo, we kindly request that you [b]report [/b]them via Redmine by following the provided instructions at this [url=https://redmine.thqnordic.com/news/26]link[/url].  
[*] If you experience a [b]crash[/b], you should also receive a prompt asking you if the information about the crash can be forwarded to us. Please do so. This information will be critical for us to address the issue. 
[/list]
To come to the point, [b]we are aware of the problems and are diligently working to address them before the game's official release[/b] planned for November 28. We will update even the Demo build itself. 

We are now fully focused on optimization and bug fixing, and our goal is to deliver a stable game that will run smoothly on machines with hardware that matches our performance requirements. 

Thank you for your patience and cooperation.

notes.title: Dev Diary #4: Worldbuilding in Last Train Home
notes.notes:
[h2]Fellow Legionaries,[/h2]

Welcome to our fourth [b]Dev Diary[/b], granting you an exclusive peek behind the curtains of the creating process of [b]Last Train Home[/b] - a survival strategy game inspired by real events. In this Dev Diary, we shall delve into the intricacies of the game's [b]worldbuilding[/b].

 [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237776/622210d70820dd68d897dcbf8db131dde7ca5a25.png[/img]
[h3]Step Into the World [/h3]

In Last Train Home, you embark on the desperate journey of [b]Czechoslovak Legionaries[/b] returning home after World War I on board an armored train. You'll be immersed in a [b]rugged[/b] and [b]sparsely populated world[/b] only slightly affected by human intervention. You'll pass mainly villages and small towns surrounded by fields and cities that have yet to embrace heavy industrialization. 

The territory is divided into very different [b]biomes[/b]. In the west, you'll be greeted by lush, verdant landscapes and even sunflower fields, a sight to behold. As you venture eastward, however, the scenery turns increasingly [b]hostile[/b], with resilient vegetation, such as larches or firs, dominating the landscape. With each kilometer you traverse, [b]the struggle for survival intensifies[/b], and the environment mirrors this growing challenge. 

It's crucial to emphasize that every [b]map [/b]and [b]view [/b]in the game is [b]handcrafted[/b]; nothing is automatically generated. Moreover, quality and quantity go hand in hand, as the average journey on board Last Train Home spans a gripping [b]40 hours[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237776/ae560a1ba9fc4fab3d3c2c385bed836472067e35.png[/img]
[h3]Diligent Research [/h3]

Given that Last Train Home takes inspiration from historical events, our Level Designers and Artists embarked on an extensive research expedition to recreate a [b]realistic in-game world[/b].  

They discovered the [b]historical train tracks[/b] within Russian territory during that era, meticulously documenting the surroundings, including the types of [b]vegetation [/b]that thrived in the extensive area. The team also uncovered the [b]original names [/b]of cities and villages along the railway, in addition to delving into the period's industry, agriculture, construction materials, or architectural styles. 

Drawing from this wealth of information, our Level Designers crafted a prototype of the fictional journey undertaken by Last Train Home while the Art Department breathed life into a visually stunning rendition of this world. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237776/aefd9f5f9158fa7a6e9182add1ef3bf6e7a713e7.png[/img]
[h3]Different types of views [/h3]

Last Train Home uniquely combines[b] real-time strategy missions [/b]and [b]train management[/b]. Thus, we constructed both the world in the missions and the world through which the train travels. In addition to the [b]Mission View[/b], you'll have two other perspectives at your disposal for train management between missions: [b]Train View[/b] and [b]Map View[/b]. 

The [b]Train View[/b] offers an up-close, zoomed-in perspective, allowing you to observe and manage individual train cars and crew members. 

On the contrary, the [b]Map View[/b] presents a zoomed-out view, enabling you to explore the expansive world and deploy your squad to various Points of Interest. This view was modeled after reality, with [b]satellite images[/b] as our primary reference.  

Naturally, some [b]adjustments[/b] were made, particularly regarding [b]the scale [/b]of objects lining the tracks. In the initial iteration, the landscape closely mirrored the original imagery, resulting in miniature hills and trees. Our goal was for the Map View to evoke the sensation of a hot air balloon ride, offering a detailed view of the landscape, so the scale needed to be adjusted. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237776/b8aca22063c6056eaa70f916fdff8b9f04efe2c3.png[/img]
[h3]Missions[/h3] 

Our missions, while rooted in reality to a degree, were designed with a touch of [b]creative liberty[/b]. The aim was to capture the romantic essence of reality, striving for authenticity without sacrificing visual appeal. Inspiration was drawn from a variety of sources, including historical photographs or the artwork of Russian landscape painter Sergey Basov. 

The missions are situated either in [b]villages[/b], characterized by modest homes of ordinary people and dominant churches, or in [b]cities[/b], where the local architectural elements reflect influences from the Old Believers Church, the Russian Revival style, and the National Romantic style. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237776/763e46183beaf62b1457f6b0813c3593f881bfbc.png[/img]
[h3]Design Process [/h3]

The mission creation process was diverse. In some instances, Level Designers envisioned a location first, weaving captivating objectives into the environment as they built it. In other cases, the process was just the opposite.  

Bringing a real-world representation into a game requires multiple [b]adjustments [/b]to enhance the visual appeal and gameplay functionality. In Last Train Home, this included altering the proportions of [b]fields [/b]and [b]rivers[/b], as maintaining their actual size would have overwhelmed the mission map. The same applied to the placement of [b]city monuments[/b] deliberately brought closer together for gameplay purposes. Another departure from historical accuracy was the abundance of [b]fences [/b]around houses, a rarity during that era but vital for providing cover for soldiers. 

One of the greatest challenges was differentiating all the locations from one another because the settlements of that era often shared similar appearances. We tried to make the characters of the cities and villages unique and memorable. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237776/51888a43305172b61b9ac092e950c803aec4938e.jpg[/img]
[h3]Creative Expression[/h3] 

Our Level Designers enjoyed overcoming the obstacles connected to choosing a historical setting. Although the time and place were pre-defined, it allowed for creative expression and proved to be [b]unexpectedly creative work[/b] for them. They saw it as a positive, enriching challenge. 

On the other hand, for our Artists, it occasionally entailed reining in their creativity and resisting the temptation to make everything as aesthetically pleasing as possible. For instance, they envisioned machine guns as much better looking than their historical counterparts. Despite that, they were pleased to see [b]the process of shaping the in-game world[/b], to play with the details, and to observe how everything eventually comes together.   

Learning about this territory and a completely unknown chapter of history was [b]fascinating[/b], and we are happy to show you, the players, how we adapted it into our game. We sincerely hope you'll appreciate our approach to crafting this world and thoroughly enjoy the experience of exploration it offers. 
 
Soon enough, it will be your turn to explore the world of Last Train Home and see for yourself. 
Stay tuned!

notes.title: Frequently Asked Questions about Last Train Home
notes.notes:
[h2]Greetings, Legionaries![/h2]

We've compiled answers to frequently asked questions about our upcoming survival strategy [b] Last Train Home[/b]. We hope you will find them useful. Should any further inquiries arise, please feel free to reach out to us via comments or our [url=https://discord.gg/lasttrain]Discord server[/url].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237776/51888a43305172b61b9ac092e950c803aec4938e.jpg[/img]

[h2]What is Last Train Home about?
[/h2]
Last Train Home is an epic survival strategy game inspired by real historical events.  
 
[i]The Great War is over, but the fight continues. Command a legion of soldiers desperately trying to make their way home amidst the chaos of civil war. Lead them through the unforgiving wilderness onboard an armored train. Manage your crew and resources and try to survive. [/i]

[h2]What will you get to experience in the game? [/h2]

[list]
[*] [b]Pick your battles:[/b] Deploy your squad and complete diverse objectives in a series of real-time missions where specialist combat skills, planning, and superior tactics will lead you to victory. 

[*] [b]Equip your soldiers:[/b] Level up your men by unlocking new skills and gathering better equipment – discover their stories, assign medals, and help them rise up through the ranks. 

[*] [b]Manage your crew:[/b] Direct your soldiers in their non-combat roles onboard the train. Craft items, heal your wounded, and restore morale for the arduous journey home. 

[*] [b]Upgrade your train: [/b]Unlock your armored train’s full potential by upgrading the carriages and locomotive and oversee important maintenance work to keep it running. 

[*][b] Journey through Siberia: [/b]Stockpile and trade supplies, make new allies, and overcome crisis after crisis as civil war rages across the vast snowfields of Siberia. 

[*] [b]Based on historical events: [/b]The Last Train Home is a compelling narrative that portrays the experiences of the Czechoslovak Legion and their valiant fight on behalf of the Entente powers during World War I. 
[/list]

[h2]What is the genre?[/h2] 

Last Train Home is a survival strategy that poses a unique combination of real-time strategy missions and train management part. 

[h2]To what extent will the story stick with historical events? [/h2]

The game is inspired by real events; it is not a historical recreation. If you want to know how we adapted the compelling story of Czechoslovak Legion to fit into our game, we encourage you to read our [url=https://thqn.net/3DRtTfl]Dev Diary[/url] dedicated to the topic.  

[h2]Will it be multiplayer?[/h2]

We’re focusing on single player experience. 

[h2]Is it going to be a sandbox game? [/h2]

No, it is a story-driven, linear game with multiple route choices. 

[h2]How long is the gameplay going to be? [/h2]

Prepare for a long journey, as the average time to beat the game is 40 hours.  

[h2]Which engine are you using?[/h2] 

We develop Last Train Home on Unreal Engine 4. 

[h2]When will it be released? [/h2]

The release is planned for 2023. We will share details as soon as we can. 

[h2]Will the game be released for consoles? 
[/h2]

It is not planned at this moment.  

[h2]Will the game have a Czech voice-over? [/h2]

Yes. Furthermore, we’re working on an immersive voice-over mode, incorporating both Slovak and Russian languages into the experience. 

[h2]Which localizations are planned?  [/h2]

[b]Text localization: [/b] English, Czech, French, German, Spanish, Portuguese (Brazil), Traditional Chinese, Simplified Chinese, Japanese, Polish, Russian 
[b]Voice Over Localization:[/b]  English, Czech, French, German 

[h2]Are you considering a physical edition? [/h2]

Yes, we are considering it. We will share further information via our channels as soon as we can.

notes.title: Dev Diary #3: Czechoslovak Legionaries: History vs. Last Train Home
notes.notes:
[h2]Greetings Legionaries, [/h2]

Welcome to our third [b]Dev Diary[/b], a behind-the-scenes glimpse into the creation of[b] Last Train Home[/b], a survival strategy game about [b]Czechoslovak Legionaries[/b] and their arduous journey back home after the Great War. In this Dev Diary, we'll delve into the [b]historical events[/b] and uncover [b]how we adapted the compelling story[/b] to fit seamlessly into our game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237776/23292411c4088d4d7abe03e0f7e7cae75c2625d7.png[/img]

[h3]Aftermath of the Great War [/h3]

The Czechoslovak Legion, which included expatriate Czech and Slovaks, was originally formed to support the Allied efforts against the Central Powers during the Great War, but circumstances soon changed. With the collapse of the Austro-Hungarian Empire and the end of the war, these soldiers found themselves [b]stranded in Russian territory[/b]. 

Consequently, the Czechoslovak Legionaries embarked on a [b]remarkable journey back home[/b]. These brave soldiers, struggling through treacherous terrains and facing daunting challenges, displayed unwavering determination to return to their newly independent homeland.  

However, instead of returning immediately, they became caught up in the [b]Russian Civil War[/b], a complex and multifaceted conflict involving various factions. The Legionaries’ military skills and discipline made them a formidable force, and they gained a reputation as a tenacious and influential group within the conflict. As they fought their way back through Siberia and other parts of Russia, they faced not only military adversaries but also logistical hardships, disease, and political complications.
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237776/5b60ed4ee69870908b28df0d5a75c8009a2824bd.jpg[/img]

[h3]Dominion over Trans-Siberian Railway  [/h3]

Fortunately, the Legionaries managed to gain control over significant portions of the [b]Trans-Siberian Railway[/b], which played a crucial role in their quest to return home. They realized that controlling the strategic railway would be vital for securing their safe passage. This control provided the Legionaries with a lifeline for supplies, transportation, and communication, critical for their survival and eventual evacuation. 

Their authority over key stretches of the Trans-Siberian Railway began in mid-1918. As the Legionaries continued to push eastward through Siberia, they encountered [b]resistance from various factions[/b] vying for control of the railway. The Bolsheviks, seeking to consolidate their power, were keen to disarm and demobilize the Legionaries. Tensions escalated, leading to armed conflicts between the Legionaries and the [b]Red Army[/b], the military force of the Bolshevik government. By mid-1919, the situation had become increasingly perilous. 

The Legionaries' hold over the Trans-Siberian Railway attracted the attention of the Allied powers, who saw the potential of utilizing their presence to support the anti-Bolshevik cause. This led to [b]complex negotiations [/b]between the Legionaries, the Allies, and the Bolshevik government regarding their safe evacuation. 

Ultimately, the Legionaries [b]succeeded in securing safe passage[/b] through the Trans-Siberian Railway, thanks to a combination of military prowess, diplomatic efforts, and shifting alliances. The railway served as a symbol of their determination and resilience. Their involvement in the Russian Civil War and their control over the Trans-Siberian Railway left an indelible mark on their historical legacy.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237776/d02af2ad2c60f119946b72e2cbeea710543b5b57.jpg[/img]

[h3]In-game adaptation of the historical events [/h3]

Primarily, we must state that Last Train Home embodies [b]a game inspired by real events[/b]. It is [b]not a historical recreation[/b]. In the subsequent passages, we shall delve into the implications of this approach for the game's narrative. 

The arduous journey of the Legionaries to the new republic entailed the movement of a staggering [b]70 thousand individuals aboard multiple trains[/b], a grueling expedition that spanned three years to culminate. Amidst this odyssey, Legionaries and their families had to somehow live their lives. Hence, they even built factories or schools alongside the Trans-Siberian Railway—a testament to their resilience and adaptability. 

To portray these historical events within the framework of a [b]strategic survival game[/b] (carrying certain technical limitations), we had to use [b]artistic license[/b] and adapt the story. Consequently, the game's focus narrowed, centering on the [b]one last fictional train[/b] taking the Legionaries back to their homeland.  

Therefore, the game does not represent how the events exactly rolled out; rather, [b]it represents what it was like to be a Czechoslovak Legionary [/b]and how it felt to lead them and make hard decisions to get them home safely. The ultimate aim of the game is to deliver a[b] deeply personal and immersive experience[/b] for the players, enveloping them in the sheer desperation of the journey. 

To achieve this ambitious goal, in 2022, we joined forces with the [b]Association of Czechoslovak Legionnaires[/b], and they provided us with expert consultations. Those were not centered on the events that historically unfolded but more on the daily lives and operations of the Legions. In other words, it was more about “How” than “What” has happened. The discussions significantly enriched our understanding of the contextual situations and conditions of the era. This knowledge influenced various aspects of the game, such as the precise portrayal of soldiers holding their weapons, both within the gameplay and in the trailers, as well as the meticulous reconstruction of train models. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237776/51888a43305172b61b9ac092e950c803aec4938e.jpg[/img]

[h3]Historical figures [/h3]

The characters were also affected by our decision. While drawing inspiration from real individuals who partook in this journey, we refrained from attempting a one-to-one representation of historical figures. In the heroic story stood out a handful of legendary characters. One of them was [b]Captain Langer[/b], who is one of the most important characters of the title. He stands by the side of the player, and he assumes a pivotal role as the player's advisor. 

However, most of the Legionaries were just ordinary people. Farmers, craftsmen, recruits with diverse (and sometimes shady) backgrounds. They had flaws, just like normal human beings do. That’s what we try to capture in the game as well, using, for example, an elaborate trait system. All that means that the players must navigate and work with [b]realistically flawed soldiers[/b] rather than an invincible heroic squad. 

We also decided to take an artistic license regarding the involvement of [b]women[/b], as the Czechoslovak Legion formally did not allow them to become soldiers. However, historical evidence attests to the presence of women on the trains, with some even engaging in combat and earning significant military honors, albeit without formal recognition as Legionary members. Consequently, we opted to include women as part of the players' forces, a decision that aligns with historical reality while acknowledging their integral contributions. 

Certain adjustments to the [b]train route[/b] were also deemed necessary to ensure a cohesive gameplay experience and facilitate accessibility for players less familiar with the historical and geographical context of the setting. Nonetheless, the majority of train stops along the journey stick with reality.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237776/69acef75a2ea170cb74405faae99e148c4a0b263.jpg[/img]

The whole game is interwoven with [b]references to events[/b] that actually happened in the era. And even though it was not possible to reflect on every interesting moment that happened during this extraordinary odyssey, we have endeavored to incorporate most of the key events into the [b] in-game encyclopedia[/b], providing players with a comprehensive experience of this remarkable historical chapter. 

We genuinely hope you've savored this sneak peek into the world of our game. Feel free to ask any lingering questions you may have.

[b]If you want to learn more about the gameplay very soon, make sure to tune in to the eagerly awaited THQ Nordic Digital Showcase 2023 on Friday, August 11.[/b]  

And if you’d like to know more about Legionaries, check out [url=https://youtu.be/Ih7FcT5mBRM]this video[/url] or [url=https://youtu.be/r10Yt_8Umrw ]this one[/url]. 

Stay tuned!

Ashborne Games

notes.title: Announcement month is behind us: How did it all roll out?
notes.notes:
[h2][h3]Hello, Legionaries! [/h3][/h2]

June was huge for us, so let's look back and [b]review the month[/b]. Are you interested in what exciting events have occurred regarding the [b]Last Train Home [/b]game? Read the article and find out. 

[h3]Last Train Home has left the station [/h3]

On 11 June, we officially announced an epic survival strategy game Last Train Home, coming to PC in 2023. Our [url=https://youtu.be/q0lJ9A4AtFo]announcement trailer[/url] had an exclusive world premiere during the [b]PC Gaming Show[/b].  

The game is inspired by the [b]Czechoslovak Legionaries'[/b] struggle to make their way home after the Great War, which is - sadly - not a very well-known chapter of history. To our happiness, we have received highly positive feedback from people worldwide. Our sincere gratitude goes to everyone who expressed their opinion about the game via any means of communication and even wishlisted our game on [url=http://www.thqn.net/lth-steam]Steam[/url]. It means a lot to us! 

[h3]Boost for the reveal: Press preview & Game Access conference [/h3]

Two more affairs were connected to the announcement of the game. 

First, we presented Last Train Home to the press. We hosted online conferences and organized [b]an exclusive press preview [/b] at the Art Cinema in Brno, CZ, to achieve that. The event occurred on 1 June, ten days before the official announcement - so we had to be super careful to keep the information about the game private.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237776/535296824cf5e9e7b1f3ba985ea24e760416d974.jpg[/img]

A special guest also attended the event - the award-winning actor [b]Karel Dobrý[/b], who plays Captain Langer in the trailers and the game itself. It was an exciting afternoon, and it certainly lifted everyone's spirits! 

Right after that, the [b]Game Access conference[/b] in Brno kicked off. We took this opportunity and presented our game as an [b]"Unannounced Project"[/b] there. People who visited the booth we shared with Nine Rocks Games studio had an exclusive chance to play [b]a short demo [/b]of Last Train Home, which included only one RTS mission. notes.title: Behind the Scenes of Last Train Home Announcement Trailer
notes.notes:
[h3]Dear Legionaries,[/h3]

we recently announced [b]Last Train Home[/b], a survival strategy game in which players lead a group of Czechoslovakian soldiers back home in the aftermath of World War I. We had an exclusive opportunity to present our [url=https://youtu.be/q0lJ9A4AtFo]Announcement trailer[/url] during the PC Gaming Show on 11 June. 
 
Let us take one step further and share details about [b]how this trailer came about[/b]. To give you an inside look, we prepared a [b]behind-the-scenes video[/b] about the filmmaking process. What may interest you is that [b]even the game's developers appeared in the trailer[/b] as soldiers freezing in action. Enjoy the show! 
 
[previewyoutube=2gXYBEk_TAc;full][/previewyoutube]
 
[h2][h1]How was the trailer created? [/h1][/h2]
 
Because our upcoming game is based on [b]historical events[/b], we had the unique opportunity to utilize [b]an existing functional replica of an armored train[/b] called [b]Legiovlak[/b]. This particular train even travels around the Czech Republic and serves as a museum on wheels, which helped to spark the idea. We also felt that a [b]live-action trailer[/b] would be the best way to capture the story and convey the proper emotions to the viewers. 
 
Four parties participated in the preparation of the trailer:  

[list]
[*] [b]Ashborne Games (the developer)[/b]: We organized the filmmaking, and members of our studio participated in the shooting as extras.
[*][b] THQ Nordic (the publisher)[/b]: Randis Albion, Senior Art Director at THQ Nordic, became the Director of Photography for the trailer. 
[*] [b]Czechoslovak Legionary Community (ČsOL)[/b]: A Czech non-profit association that we consulted regarding the historical accuracy of the game narrative and the trailer (e. g. the used replicas of weapons, clothing, relics, etc.). Many of them are descendants of Czechoslovak legionaries. They allowed us to use the train and appeared as extras in the trailer. 
[*] [b]Gnomon Production[/b]: A Czech film production company founded in Brno, which has produced live-action videos and documentary films since 2009. 
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237776/02223e5012f6509d42eabf3f04770d0baaa64e4c.jpg[/img]

Apart from the developers, the trailer includes real actors, such as award-winning Czech actor [b]Karel Dobrý[/b] [Mission: Impossible, A Knight's Tale, Carnival Row, and many more], who portrays [b]Captain Langer[/b]. You may as well get acquainted with his appearance because he represents this character even [b]in the game[/b]. He’s the one that will lead you through the story as your advisor.  

Many of you already reached out to us and expressed your liking for the trailer. Our heartfelt gratitude goes to everyone who did so and even supported us by adding the game to their wishlist on [url=thqn.net/lth-steam]Steam[/url]. 

If you’re interested in learning more, follow us on our social media and join the discussion on our Discord server. Thanks to the filming, we have much material to show you in the future, including other trailer(s). 😉

notes.title: Last Train Home is coming your way!
notes.notes:
Gaming studio [b]Ashborne Games[/b], a proud member of the [b]THQ Nordic[/b] family, is happy to announce a new epic survival strategy game inspired by real historical events: [b]Last Train Home[/b]. 

If you haven't had a chance to catch the world premiere of our announcement trailer during the PC Gaming show, watch it now! 

[previewyoutube=q0lJ9A4AtFo;full][/previewyoutube]

[h1]What is Last Train Home about? [/h1]

[i]The Great War is over, but the fight continues. Command a legion of soldiers desperately trying to make their way home amidst the chaos of civil war. Lead them through the unforgiving wilderness onboard an armored train. Manage your crew and resources, and try to survive. [/i]

[h1]What will you get to experience as a legionary? [/h1]

[list]
[*][b] Pick your battles: [/b]Deploy your squad and complete diverse objectives in a series of real-time missions where specialist combat skills, planning, and superior tactics will lead you to victory. 
[*] [b]Equip your soldiers:[/b] Level up your men by unlocking new skills and gathering better equipment – discover their stories, assign medals, and help them rise up through the ranks. 
[*] [b]Manage your crew:[/b] Direct your soldiers in their non-combat roles onboard the train. Craft items, heal your wounded, and restore morale for the arduous journey home. 
[*] [b]Upgrade your train: [/b]Unlock your armored train’s full potential by upgrading the carriages and locomotive and oversee important maintenance work to keep it running. 
[*] [b]Journey through Siberia: [/b]Stockpile and trade supplies, make new allies, and overcome crisis after crisis as civil war rages across the vast snowfields of Siberia.  
[*] [b]Based on historical events:[/b] The Last Train Home is a compelling narrative that portrays the experiences of the Czechoslovak Legion and their valiant fight on behalf of the Entente powers during World War I. 
[/list]

[url=thqn.net/lth-steam][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237776/9337c92cd220e3da1283245f0cd198faeda7d8d1.png[/img][/url]
